### 🎯 Practical Learning Objectives (Week 11)

This week is a **revision and integration** of what you have learned so far. By the end of this practical session, you should be able to:

- **Formulate** a simple **data science question** from a real or sample dataset.
- **Carry out** basic **EDA** (loading, cleaning, summarising, visualising).
- **Apply** at least **one analysis or model** you have seen before (correlation, regression, clustering, association rules, hypothesis test, simple prediction).
- **Interpret** results in **plain language** and connect them to a real-world context.
- **Document** your work clearly in a **notebook-style report**.

> 💡 Think of this as a **mini-project** that brings together ideas from Weeks 1–10. In the course outline: *"Mini-project – predictive modelling, data mining, and BI dashboard development."*

> 📌 **How this notebook works.** The notebook is already filled in with a **worked example** on the `heart.csv` data so that every chunk runs. You will **replace the dataset, variables and interpretation with your own**. The worked example shows the *method*, not the answer to your project.

## 1. Choosing Your Dataset and Question

For this mini-project you may use:

- A dataset provided by your lecturer (recommended), from the `data` folder.
- A small open dataset (students' performance, sales records, survey responses).
- A dataset you used in previous weeks (the cleaned version).

| File in `data/` | One row is... | Example numeric variables | Example categorical / binary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `heart.csv` | a patient (anonymised) | `age`, `trestbps`, `chol`, `thalach` | `sex`, `cp`, `target` |
| `titanic_clean.csv` | a passenger | `Age`, `Fare` | `Survived`, `Pclass`, `Sex` |
| `advertising.csv` | a website user | `Age`, `Area Income`, `Daily Internet Usage` | `Male`, `Clicked on Ad` |
| `student_score.csv` | a student | `Hours`, `Scores` | – |
| `amazon_products_clean.csv` | a product | `actual_price`, `discount_pct`, `rating` | `main_category` |
| `retail_sales_ng.csv` (synthetic) | a sales transaction | `Sales_Amount`, `Quantity`, `Profit` | `Region`, `Product_Category` |
| `grocery_transactions.csv` (synthetic) | an item in a basket | – | `Item` (use association rules) |
| `data.csv` | a breast-tissue sample | `radius_mean`, `texture_mean`, ... | `diagnosis` |

## 2. Loading Required Packages

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# Helper: regression metrics used in Week 5
metrics <- function(y, yhat) {
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean((y - yhat)^2)),
    MAE  = mean(abs(y - yhat)),
    R2   = 1 - sum((y - yhat)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2))
}
```

## 4. Light Data Cleaning

Before analysis we may need to handle **missing values**, remove **duplicates**, and convert **data types**. Use only what your dataset needs: do not over-clean.

```{r missing}
colSums(is.na(df))                 # missing values per column
```

```{r duplicates}
duplicates_count <- sum(duplicated(df))
cat("Number of duplicate rows:", duplicates_count, "\n")

df <- distinct(df)                 # keep one copy of each row
cat("New shape after removing duplicates:", dim(df), "\n")
```

> ℹ️ Examples of other cleaning steps (edit and use if needed):
> `df <- drop_na(df, ImportantColumn)` · `df <- mutate(df, Col = replace_na(Col, median(Col, na.rm = TRUE)))` · `df <- mutate(df, Date = as.Date(Date))`

## 5. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

Now explore the data in relation to your **main question**. Suggested steps:

- Look at **distributions** (histograms, boxplots) of key numerical variables.
- Look at **counts** (bar charts) for important categorical variables.
- Examine **relationships** (scatter plots, group means, correlations).

### 5.1 Distributions of Numerical Variables

```{r hist}
num_col <- "thalach"          # TODO: change to a numeric variable related to your question

ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[num_col]])) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 25, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  geom_density(colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = paste("Distribution of", num_col), x = num_col, y = "Density")
```

### 5.2 Frequency of a Categorical Variable

```{r bar}
cat_col <- "target"           # TODO: change to a categorical variable

ggplot(df, aes(x = factor(.data[[cat_col]]))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(stat = "count", aes(label = after_stat(count)), vjust = -0.4) +
  labs(title = paste("Counts of", cat_col), x = cat_col, y = "Count")
```

### 5.3 Relationship Between Two Numerical Variables

```{r scatter}
x_col <- "age"                # TODO: change
y_col <- "thalach"            # TODO: change

pair_df <- df |> select(all_of(c(x_col, y_col))) |> drop_na()

ggplot(pair_df, aes(x = .data[[x_col]], y = .data[[y_col]])) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = paste(y_col, "versus", x_col), x = x_col, y = y_col)

ct <- cor.test(pair_df[[x_col]], pair_df[[y_col]])
cat(sprintf("Correlation between %s and %s: r = %.3f, 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], p = %s\n",
            x_col, y_col, ct$estimate, ct$conf.int[1], ct$conf.int[2], format.pval(ct$p.value, digits = 3)))
```
